speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether the Government’s position is that non-vulnerable Singaporeans should continue to get their booster shots to keep their vaccination against COVID-19 current; and (b) how long more will Singaporeans continue to be able to get their booster shots free-of-charge.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether an update can be provided on the Ministry's review of the remaining post-COVID-19 measures currently in place such as the mask-wearing requirement in healthcare settings; (b) whether there are plans to modify this measure to make mask-wearing non-mandatory in healthcare settings; and (c) if so, when will this change take place.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: My response will also cover the matters raised in the written question by Ms Joan Pereira.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: However, we have also adjusted our normal time practices, such as requiring mask wearing in patient-facing settings, to better protect patients and healthcare workers from respiratory infectious diseases in general, not just for COVID-19.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) will continue to monitor the broader communicable disease situation, review our disease control practices and adjust our approach.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The latest variants of interests are EG.5 and BA.2.86, which have a number of additional mutations compared with previous Omicron variants.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Fortunately, so far, the science and empirical evidence show that existing vaccines continue to accord good protection against severe illness for individuals.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The pharmaceutical industry continues to update COVID-19 vaccines to preserve the effectiveness against new variants.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: For example, Pfizer’s latest vaccine specifically targets XBB1.5.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Our contracts with suppliers enable us to procure the latest vaccines once they are assessed to be appropriate for the local situation.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Expert Committee on COVID-19 Vaccination is currently reviewing the data of the updated Comirnaty vaccine and will be providing its recommendations.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will share more details when operational arrangements are confirmed.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are able to achieve DORSCON Green not because COVID-19 became a mild disease.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is still a dangerous virus, especially for our vulnerable individuals and seniors.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We can live with the virus now because our resilience has strengthened due to vaccinations and safe recovery from infections.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: MOH will continue to monitor the situation closely.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will take into account expert advice, the latest evidence and will update our recommendations on the basis of those, as needed.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I would just like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether, in his opinion, there is vaccination fatigue now, whether the vaccination rate is dropping partly because people are feeling it is much safer now and also for fear of the side-effects of vaccination.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: If so, what is MOH's strategy to deal with this vaccination fatigue and whether there is a long-term plan, like what the Senior Minister of State just mentioned?
